title: Mushroom Swiss Steak Pan
seoTitle: Mushroom Swiss Steak Pan | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Seared round steak with mushrooms and Swiss over mashed potatoes for ten
subtitle: Seared round steak with mushrooms and Swiss over mashed potatoes for ten
description: Sirloin strips sear fast, simmer with mushrooms and onions in a rich broth base, then finish off heat with sour cream for a silky sauce. Serve over wide egg noodles with parsley.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Mushroom Swiss Steak Pan in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.instruction: Pat sirloin strips dry and season with salt and pepper. Sear in butter over high heat in batches 30–45 seconds per side until browned but still pink inside. Set aside.

steps.title: Cook mushrooms and onion
steps.instruction: In the same pot, sauté mushrooms and onion 8 minutes until moisture evaporates and edges brown. Add garlic and cook 1 minute. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.instruction: Pour in beef broth and simmer 5 minutes, scraping fond from the bottom. Whisk Dijon into sour cream, then stir off heat into the warm broth until smooth.

steps.title: Cook the noodles
steps.instruction: Boil egg noodles in salted water until al dente, about 8 minutes. Drain and toss with a tablespoon of butter. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Mushroom Swiss Steak Pan onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Combine and serve
steps.instruction: Return beef and any juices to sauce and warm 2 minutes—do not boil. Serve noodles topped with stroganoff and parsley at the line. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Partially freeze sirloin 20 minutes for easier thin slicing.
If sauce breaks, whisk in a spoonful of cold sour cream off heat to bring it back.
Frozen peas stirred in at the end add color and stretch the dish cheaply.
tonightSpread: Stroganoff over noodles with crusty bread for sauce mopping.
Simple cucumber salad with dill for a cool contrast.
leftovers: Reheat gently with splash of broth—microwave on medium, not full blast.
Fill baked potato skins with stroganoff and melted cheese.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Stroganoff is pure comfort after cold calls. The sauce feels indulgent but comes together in one pot plus a noodle boil—manageable even for newer cooks.
mealPrepNotes: Slice beef against the grain thin for tender bites. Stir sour cream off heat so it does not break. Hold sauce and noodles separately if holding more than 30 minutes.
